title: Fix Global Ranking System visibility, sorting, and weekly snapshot logic

requirements.text: Remove any device-specific or caller-only ranking behavior so the Rank screen always loads a truly global leaderboard from the Internet Computer canister (not from local cache/state), and ensure no code path filters rankings down to the current user only.

quotes: All users are NOT visible to each other. Ranking is either device-specific, partially loaded, or incorrectly filtered.
Remove any ranking logic based on: Local storage ... Current-user-only filtering
Remove any query like: where user_id == current_user_id

acceptanceCriteria: With at least 3 different authenticated users, each user can open Rank and see all users (not only themselves).
No fetch call used by the Rank screen applies a filter that restricts results to the current caller.

Local storage / IndexedDB / in-memory app state is not used as the primary ranking source; if any cache is used, it is only a stale fallback when the canister cannot be reached and must be clearly labeled stale in UI.

requirements.text: Upgrade the backend ranking data contract to expose all public ranking fields required by the UI for every user: user_id, name, college, total_points, current_streak, longest_streak, and join_date, and ensure the backend returns global results for all users (no per-caller filtering).

quotes: Each document must contain: user_id name college total_points current_streak longest_streak join_date
Every logged-in user must fetch ALL users

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes a leaderboard query that returns entries containing: userId (or equivalent stable identifier), displayName/name, college, totalPoints, currentStreak, longestStreak, joinDate for every visible user.
The returned leaderboard data is global (derived from the canister’s full user set), not scoped to the caller.
No backend query used for leaderboard applies an unintended filter (e.g., by caller, by college substring in name, etc.).

requirements.text: Correct rank calculation to be deterministic and computed at runtime from the full global dataset using the exact tie-breakers: total_points (descending), longest_streak (descending), join_date (ascending), and assign rank = index + 1 without persisting a static rank value as user data.

quotes: Assign ranks dynamically: For index i in sorted list: rank = i + 1
Do NOT store static rank in database. Rank must be calculated at runtime.

acceptanceCriteria: Given sample data (User A 100 points, User B 150 points, User C 80 points), all devices/users see ranks: 1 User B, 2 User A, 3 User C.
Ranks in the returned list are strictly increasing 1..N with no missing numbers and no duplicates.
If two users have equal total points, the user with higher longest streak ranks above; if still tied, the earlier join date ranks above.
Reopening the app without any backend data changes does not change ordering or rank numbers.

requirements.text: Fix pagination/incremental loading so that the Rank screen can scale to 100+ users without truncation, while still ensuring the UI can load and render the complete global ranking list (either via repeated page fetches until exhaustion or via an explicit 'load more' flow).

quotes: Display ALL users in scrollable list. No truncation. No limit unless pagination for 100+ users.

acceptanceCriteria: For N users (including N > 100), the UI can render all users in correct rank order (1..N) without truncation.
If pagination is used, fetching subsequent pages does not change earlier ranks and does not create duplicate/missing ranks.
Scrolling remains smooth and the layout does not overflow or jank with large lists.

requirements.text: Ensure the Rank UI highlights the current logged-in user reliably (even if other users share the same display name) and auto-scrolls them into view when they are not in the Top 3.
acceptanceCriteria: Current user highlight does not rely on displayName equality alone; it uses a stable user identifier from the backend (e.g., principal/user_id) to identify the row.
When the Rank screen opens and the current user is not in the Top 3, the list auto-scrolls to the highlighted row.
If multiple users have the same name, only the correct current user row is highlighted and labeled “You”.

requirements.text: Implement and/or correct weekly ranking snapshot/rollover logic so weekly recalculation does not run multiple times unnecessarily: store a last_update_date (or equivalent timestamp) and only recalculate when the local time condition matches the chosen weekly boundary (Sunday 12:00 AM) and the last update is older than the current weekly boundary.

quotes: If weekly ranking is used: • Do NOT duplicate recalculation multiple times. • Store last_update_date. • Recalculate only if current day is Sunday AND last_update_date is older.

acceptanceCriteria: Backend stores a single authoritative last ranking update timestamp (or last snapshotted week marker) in stable state.
Weekly ranking recalculation is idempotent: repeated calls within the same week do not create duplicate snapshots or inconsistent results.
A week boundary rollover triggers at most one recalculation per week boundary and produces deterministic rankings based on the tie-breaker rules.

requirements.text: Preserve near-real-time leaderboard updates without WebSockets by ensuring polling/refetching is safe (no memory leaks) and results remain consistent across devices; do not allow cached/stale data to override fresh global results when the backend is reachable.

quotes: The corrected ranking system must: • Be real-time synced • Be consistent across all devices

acceptanceCriteria: While the Rank screen is visible, periodic refresh updates the leaderboard when backend data changes (e.g., points updates) without requiring a full app reload.
Timers/intervals are cleaned up on unmount/navigation and do not accumulate duplicate polling loops.
When backend fetch succeeds, the UI uses backend results (not cached data) and clears any stale-warning state.

requirements.text: Update all user-facing text in the ranking flow to be clear English, including explicit messaging when data is stale (cached fallback) or when the leaderboard cannot be loaded.

quotes: Use English for any user-facing text in the build request.

acceptanceCriteria: When showing cached/fallback rankings, the UI displays a clear English warning that the leaderboard may be stale.
When the leaderboard cannot be loaded and no cache exists, the UI shows a clear English error state with a retry action.
No non-English strings are introduced in the ranking-related UI.

constraints: Do not rebuild the app; implement targeted fixes to the existing ranking architecture only.
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor in backend/main.mo; introduce backend/migration.mo only if stable state schema changes require migration.
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui (read-only).

Firebase Firestore integration and security rules cannot be implemented on this platform; use the existing Internet Computer (Motoko) canister as the single global ranking source instead while achieving the same functional goals (global visibility, deterministic sorting, scalable loading).
nonGoals: Do not change any attendance tracking calculations or subject/timetable features.
Do not add third-party authentication providers; continue using Internet Identity.
Do not implement WebSockets or real-time sockets for leaderboard updates.
